shoal_e05_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_entry.text: At sunset on Day Two Hundred Sixty-Five, Song Mei's performance room smelled of lamp oil, damp coats, and sliced pears. Yue had come for a voice, but the yard's final eight-day trial still needed one last completed fact in her mind. Its schedule had changed actual working hours and the number of housing observations. She finished the permitted public tally before taking her place among people who had paid to hear someone else's story.

shoal_e05_dawn_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_dawn_01.text: The early-work trial had completed thirty-two housing observations within the source-specific unloaded scope. Eight stayed pending. No later comparison in this term would secretly fill the lost hours; its remaining shifts were assigned to owner returns, sorting, and packing. The supervisor signed that boundary after the final early setup was cleared. He called the result adequate for the revised work, not equivalent to forty. Yue could repeat that description without turning a compromise into an invisible success.

shoal_e05_dawn_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_dawn_02.text: The five packing workers had retained daytime corner use through the accepted trial. Their current collection routes had continued, while their next license still required a separate decision. The guard and moving helpers received the actual named trial pay. The comparison equipment left overnight storage under its proper owners' custody, without granting the guard a continuing technical role. The space adjustment closed with performed work and eight genuinely unanswered housing entries.

shoal_e05_dawn_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_dawn_03.text: Rong's revised delivery list withheld the eight pending parts from any claim of completed observation. He still wanted them checked later and would need a new lawful source and funded task. Yue could not offer her evenings to erase the shortage. Her exhausted mornings had shown what that offer would cost. The current supplier lost an expected comparison result; the packers kept an expected collection place. Those were the material sides of the chosen schedule.

shoal_e05_dawn_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_dawn_04.text: At the performance door, the fruit seller waved from a bench. He had paid his own ordinary ticket and brought no claim that Yue should sit with him out of gratitude. She joined the public bench nearby. The day had ended with thirty-two observations and five continued corner routes. Tonight could contain something besides defending that balance. The lodging invitations and this space trial had ended on their agreed dates; later invitations would need their own terms.

shoal_e05_day_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_day_01.text: The uninterrupted daytime plan had completed the full forty-housing observation sequence by the twenty-fifth performed shift, within each source's actual unloaded scope. Completion did not mean forty sound parts or fueled qualification. The remaining five paid shifts would prepare returns, sorting, and packing rather than invent another comparison target. The supervisor marked unresolved technical fields as unresolved, even where an exterior observation was complete. A full row count could not create answers unavailable from the offered source.

shoal_e05_day_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_day_02.text: The three willing lower-room workers had completed their eight-day trial and kept the orders they actually filled there. The two who refused had not been moved by force. Their missed corner commissions remained missed, and their later work routes were the ones they had chosen. The room rent, accepted moves, and notices were paid from the adjustment account. No balance was quietly converted into compensation the appropriation had never authorized.

shoal_e05_day_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_day_03.text: Rong's delivery list could use the forty completed observation entries under their stated limits. It still could not advertise every part as safe for fuel. He called the schedule efficient, while He Ming retained the public displacement note beside the tally. Yue wanted to defend herself and instead read both pages once more. They recorded different consequences of the same accepted hours. A larger output did not make the lost walk-up trade disappear.

shoal_e05_day_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_day_04.text: At the performance door, He Ming nodded from a bench without reserving a place for Yue. Their next conversation about packing space would need its own time. She took a public seat near the aisle. The lodging invitations and the space trial had ended on their agreed dates; no ongoing delegate role followed them. Tonight she could hear the performer without being asked to declare the daytime schedule wholly good or wholly wrong.

shoal_e05_tally_rejoin.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_tally_rejoin.text: Song Mei came out wearing a dark coat repaired at both cuffs. She had chosen the room after rejecting a keeper's claim to every future sheet sale. Here, a fixed four-copper venue fee covered the inspected evening. Two musicians would receive three copper each. Eighteen ordinary one-copper audience tickets funded the performance, with four copper committed to eight permitted sheets. Song Mei retained the remainder and her unoffered stories. Yue watched her check the door count before beginning.

shoal_e05_performance_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_01.text: The permitted room capacity included performers and staff as well as ticket holders. The keeper stopped a late group when its arrival would exceed that number. One man protested that standing did not take a seat. The attendant showed the clear exit width and refused him without asking Song Mei to interrupt her preparation. His missed performance was real, but it did not buy a narrower escape route for everyone else. Yue moved her bag under the bench as instructed.

shoal_e05_performance_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_02.text: A boy in the audience tapped the bench in anticipation of a drum. His mother asked him to stop until the musicians started. The drummer heard the rhythm and borrowed its shape for a short opening phrase, then let the child rest. No one called it a sign of hidden talent or promised an apprenticeship. The exchange made the room feel inhabited before any official story began. Yue heard a laugh from a man she had seen only arguing at public tables.

shoal_e05_performance_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_03.text: Song Mei's first piece concerned a fictional gate keeper who tried to charge the tide for entering after curfew. He spent more ink on the tide's refusal than on the gate's repairs. The audience recognized familiar habits without being handed a named official to punish. When the fictional keeper finally learned to mend a hinge, the drummer gave him a rhythm too clumsy for dignity. Song Mei waited through the laughter instead of using it to rush into her next line.

shoal_e05_performance_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_04.text: Yue could see why Song Mei had cared about the room's acoustics. A quiet consonant reached the back without being shouted, and the audience did not have to lean into the aisle. The room did not make every listener attentive. Two merchants whispered during a verse about a boat's marriage to its cargo. Song Mei glanced toward them once and continued. People had bought a performance, not surrendered their attention by contract. Their failure to listen still cost the piece something.

shoal_e05_performance_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_05.text: The second piece was older and slower. A woman in the story left a shore where everyone knew her husband and found work repairing baskets inland. She missed the harbor without returning to it. Song Mei offered no explanation that the husband had been cruel, noble, dead, or secretly immortal. The leaving had its own reasons in the woman's voice. Yue noticed how often she had expected a story to justify a woman's departure by making somebody else deserving of it.

shoal_e05_performance_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_06.text: A rigger near the back wiped a hand across his face. The movement might have cleared sweat, a tear, or lamp smoke. Yue would not know. Song Mei let the silence hold after the final line. The drummer set his hands flat on the skin instead of adding a flourish. A performance could refuse the audience's demand for an obvious feeling just as a witness could refuse to fill an unseen angle. The refusal made Yue listen harder.

shoal_e05_performance_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_07.text: Then someone near the door called out a familiar harbor name, asking whether the leaving woman represented his sister. Song Mei said the piece was fictional and belonged to a wider set of journeys. If he wanted to speak about his sister, that would be his own account and required her consent before publication. He looked embarrassed, then angry. He had heard something private in a public song. That resemblance did not give the performer ownership of his family's story.

shoal_e05_performance_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_08.text: The attendant offered him a seat nearer the exit if he wanted to step out. He chose to leave and received no ticket refund under the posted ordinary terms. Song Mei did not mock him after the door closed. The interruption had broken the piece's quiet ending, and that ending could not be replayed in precisely the same room. The musicians took the planned pause. Yue felt the real cost without needing to declare the departing man a villain.

shoal_e05_performance_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_09.text: During the pause, a woman asked whether the printed sheets contained that leaving piece. They did not. Song Mei had chosen a different permitted set, including the fictional tide keeper and a short song about repairing a coat. Her unprinted piece stayed unprinted. A ticket had bought the evening's listening, not a permanent transcript. Yue watched the woman accept the limit and ask instead whether the coat song could be read aloud at her own household table.

shoal_e05_performance_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_10.text: The sheet permission allowed that ordinary noncommercial reading of the offered text. It did not allow a workshop to claim Song Mei's future script or print private conversations she had heard in the port. The woman said she could remember the melody badly but liked the words. Song Mei said a badly remembered melody was a common visitor to household tables. The room laughed again, softly this time. The performer had recovered an audience, not the lost exact ending of her earlier piece.

shoal_e05_performance_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_11.text: The floorboard under a front stool creaked when its sitter shifted. The attendant asked the sitter to stand, inspected the loose wedge, and removed the stool from use. Another permitted seat was available without narrowing the aisle. Song Mei waited with the musicians silent. Yue stayed seated instead of catching the stool overhead or testing it with qi. The ordinary interruption took several minutes and gave the keeper a repair task before the next venue license check.

shoal_e05_performance_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_12.text: When the music resumed, Song Mei chose the coat song earlier than listed because the room needed a lighter rhythm. She had the authority to change her own program within the offered scope. A listener complained that the public notice had named another sequence. The keeper showed the note allowing that adjustment without substituting an entirely different event. A flexible performance still needed a recognizable promise. Song Mei could make a living artist's choice without calling every unhappy listener unreasonable.

shoal_e05_performance_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_13.text: The coat song's woman kept a cuff patched with a piece of her brother's discarded wedding sash. He wanted it back after the marriage failed. She said the cuff had survived more faithfully than his ceremony and offered to lend him the other sleeve. People laughed at different places. Yue laughed at the impossible lending. A packer beside her laughed at the brother. Song Mei sang on without instructing them which meaning belonged to a more enlightened audience.

shoal_e05_performance_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_14.text: At the far bench, a child began to sleep against an adult's shoulder. The adult moved the child's feet clear of the aisle and stayed. The ticket did not require the child to absorb every line. Yue felt her own fatigue settle in a harmless way, less like a warning and more like a day finally ending. She had eaten, rested after work, and kept her cleared bodily range. Enjoyment had ordinary conditions too, which no certificate could remove.

shoal_e05_performance_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_15.text: The final piece concerned a sailor who wanted his name carved on a boat he did not own. He did not steal the boat. He worked long enough to buy a small one and found that its name looked cramped on the stern. Song Mei let the story end with him painting over half the letters. Yue had expected a grander vessel or a lesson in contentment. Instead, a real ambition had met wood of a particular size.

shoal_e05_performance_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_16.text: The applause came unevenly, then strengthened as listeners recognized that the ending was intentional. The musicians stood after Song Mei, and the keeper opened the public door once the exit lane was clear. A few people asked where the next performance would be. Song Mei had no signed next room and gave no invented date. The port would remember an evening that might remain alone. A completed event did not create a continuing service merely because its audience wanted one.

shoal_e05_performance_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_17.text: Rong stayed by the sheet table and asked whether a supplier might buy the coat song for a workroom notice. Song Mei offered the current permitted text under a separately priced limited print license, subject to an actual agreement later. He could not buy the leaving piece by paying more at this table. Yue liked the absence of drama in her refusal. Song Mei had probably practiced it through many rooms that wanted to call ownership a compliment.

shoal_e05_performance_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_18.text: He Ming wanted a later reading for packers unable to leave their current work. Song Mei said she could offer a short oral reprise in a licensed small room tonight for two consenting listeners already waiting, if an ordinary assistant kept the route and door clear. Otherwise, they would need another offered date. She would not send a story into an active packing yard to compete with work instructions. He Ming went to ask the listeners what they preferred.

shoal_e05_performance_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_19.text: At the same time, the keeper could open the permitted sheet desk for a short after-performance window if it had a staffed seller. Eight printed sheets were ready under Song Mei's four-copper print expense. Without that seller, the desk would close and the sheets would remain hers, unsold tonight. Buyers might be found later, but tonight's departing audience would be gone. The keeper's staff could maintain the ordinary exit or sell papers, not both inside its agreed hours.

shoal_e05_performance_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_20.text: Song Mei offered Yue one of two two-copper bounded tasks from her own evening income. She could staff the sheet desk and follow the actual print permission, or assist the two consenting listeners' oral reprise in the licensed side room. The tasks overlapped in the available hour. Yue had no technical shift tomorrow morning, but she did need to end this work at the stated time. The offer did not make her an artist's permanent agent or require her to choose.

shoal_e05_performance_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_21.text: The two listeners had asked for an oral reprise because one could not comfortably read the small printed page and the other wanted to hear the rhythm. They could decline it if no assistant accepted. The potential sheet buyers had their own household tables and wanted a permitted text to carry away. Neither audience was less real. Song Mei could perform the offered reprise or supervise the staffed sheet sale within the same remaining hour, not stretch her voice and attention into two events.

shoal_e05_performance_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_22.text: Yue asked whether refusing both tasks would hurt their friendship. Song Mei said she would find another evening arrangement, and that a friend who could only say yes was exhausting company. Yue laughed, relieved by the sharpness. She wanted to accept one task because it interested her, not because refusal would cost her work or make their friendship conditional. The small offer contained actual wages, readers, listeners, and a missed opportunity on the other side.

shoal_e05_performance_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_23.text: The musicians had been paid their agreed three copper each after their completed parts. The keeper received the fixed four-copper venue fee. The four-copper sheet printing expense was already incurred. From eighteen ticket copper, Song Mei retained four before any accepted assistant pay or sheet sales. She showed Yue those figures because the task was her own offer. It did not draw on the restoration's wages, materials, or care reserve.

shoal_e05_performance_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_performance_24.text: Outside, the departing audience began to scatter into its own roads. There was no hidden crowd waiting to replace every missed buyer later tonight. The two oral listeners waited at the licensed side door without a promise. Song Mei stood between the desk and the side room, her hand resting on the unsold sheets. Yue could accept the paper task or the listening task. Whatever she chose, the hour would end with one offered audience served and another opportunity unperformed.

shoal_e05_art_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_art_choice.text: Song Mei offered two overlapping two-copper tasks, both ending within the hour. A staffed sheet desk could carry eight permitted texts to tonight's departing readers and earn actual sales. An assisted side-room reprise could let two consenting people hear the voice and rhythm they could not get from those sheets. The artist retained her script, choices, and unoffered stories. Yue chose the bounded task she wanted to complete.

choices.text: Staff the permitted sheet desk for tonight's readers.
Assist the side-room oral reprise for the two listeners.

shoal_e05_sheets_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_01.text: Yue accepted the sheet desk and read its offered permission once with Song Mei. Eight sheets, one copper each, carried the tide keeper and coat song for ordinary household reading. No leaving piece appeared among them. No buyer received a future print license or the right to add private harbor names beneath fictional characters. Song Mei would answer artistic questions beside the desk while Yue handled the bounded sale. The keeper opened the table only after the main exit had cleared.

shoal_e05_sheets_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_02.text: He Ming told the two oral listeners that the immediate reprise would not take place. One accepted a public contact for a possible later offered reading; the other declined because she would leave the port soon. Their unperformed hour remained unperformed. Song Mei gave no guarantee that another evening would fit both of them. Yue saw them walk away in different directions, carrying neither a purchased sheet nor the rhythm they had hoped to hear tonight.

shoal_e05_sheets_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_03.text: The first buyer was the woman who wanted to read the coat song at a household table. She counted a copper from a purse tied with old sailcloth and asked whether a child could sing the printed words to a different tune. Song Mei allowed an ordinary private household variation under the offered text's scope, without endorsing a commercial imitation. The woman looked pleased by the practical answer. Yue handed her one sheet and marked one completed sale.

shoal_e05_sheets_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_04.text: A young apprentice wanted two sheets but had only one copper left after the ticket. He chose one and said he would share it with his sister through an ordinary household reading. Yue did not give him an unauthorized extra from Song Mei's stock. The artist could decide to offer a gift herself, but the assistant's task was to honor the offered sale. The apprentice accepted the single sheet without acting as though a refusal proved the desk did not care about him.

shoal_e05_sheets_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_05.text: The third buyer asked to put his employer's name above the tide keeper as a joke. Song Mei declined that alteration under this offered permission. He still bought the unaltered sheet and said the joke would occur to readers anyway. She could not command their private thoughts, but she could refuse to print a named accusation she had not authored. Yue watched the man fold the sheet carefully. Boundaries did not always end a sale.

shoal_e05_sheets_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_06.text: At the fourth sale, a copper coin had an unfamiliar clipped edge. Yue asked Song Mei before rejecting it. The keeper's ordinary receiver checked the local acceptance mark and confirmed it remained valid at the posted value. No qi assay was needed. Yue took the coin and corrected her own count. Being responsible for a purse made her suspicious faster than she expected; an unfamiliar object still deserved a check rather than an instant story about a dishonest owner.

shoal_e05_sheets_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_07.text: Two cousins arrived together and argued over who had heard the coat song's funniest line correctly. Song Mei pointed to the actual offered text and let them disagree about why it was funny. They bought one sheet each. Yue liked that the page did not settle the argument it had helped create. A durable text could carry a performance beyond the room while losing the pause, accent, and listener's face that had made a particular line work.

shoal_e05_sheets_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_08.text: Rong bought the seventh sheet at the ordinary price and repeated his interest in a limited workroom print license. Song Mei gave him a public appointment request channel, with no acceptance tonight. His purchased copy allowed the same ordinary use as anyone else's. Paying for a sheet did not acquire a shortcut around the separate agreement. Yue could see the merchant testing whether the artist's desk worked like every other desk that sold something useful.

shoal_e05_sheets_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_09.text: The eighth buyer was a porter who had stood outside the room during the performance because the audience limit was reached. He wanted the tide keeper text, though he had missed its voice. The sheet gave him part of the evening and left another part unavailable. Song Mei read one permitted short line as he counted his copper, then stopped because the desk hour was ending. A small courtesy did not recreate the entire performance he had not heard.

shoal_e05_sheets_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_10.text: At the stated closing time, all eight sheets had sold for eight copper. Yue and Song Mei counted the money together. From the eighteen ticket copper after the fixed venue fee, musician wages, and print expense, Song Mei had retained four. The eight actual sales raised that to twelve; the completed two-copper assistant task left her ten. Yue received her two only after the count and closure were complete. No hypothetical later license payment entered that purse.

shoal_e05_sheets_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_11.text: The keeper cleared the table for its next ordinary use. Yue checked that no unsold stock or buyer's private scrap remained among the cups. A forgotten note belonged to the apprentice who had bought one sheet; the keeper kept it under its proper lost-property process rather than letting the seller read it. Song Mei carried her remaining script and sale record herself. Yue's accepted role ended at the cleared table, not at some future control of every household reading.

shoal_e05_sheets_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_12.text: Outside, the oral listeners were gone. Their offered experience had not occurred, even though eight people carried texts home. Song Mei said she might offer a later reading if her voice and the room schedule allowed it. She would not promise the listener who was leaving a date she could not meet. Yue felt the urge to fund a second event from her own wages. Song Mei asked her to let an unperformed offer remain a fact instead of a personal emergency.

shoal_e05_sheets_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_13.text: They walked a short public stretch together. Song Mei asked which buyer had made Yue nervous. Yue described the clipped coin and admitted how quickly she had imagined intent from shape. The artist said audiences did something similar with stories, seeing a resemblance and assigning a target before asking what had actually been offered. The comparison did not erase either error. It gave Yue a way to recognize her own habit the next time it felt like certainty.

shoal_e05_sheets_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_sheets_14.text: At the lane junction, Song Mei thanked her for a completed sale task and declined company farther because she wanted the remaining walk alone. Yue accepted the end without asking whether ten retained copper meant the evening had succeeded. It meant bills could be paid and some permitted texts had left the room. It did not measure the missed oral reprise, the interrupted leaving piece, or the artist's private satisfaction. Those were hers to assess.

shoal_e05_oral_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_01.text: Yue accepted the side-room task and checked its ordinary route with the keeper. The two consenting listeners would enter through the licensed public door, sit where the exit remained clear, and leave before the agreed hour ended. The room's use was included in the offered evening terms; no one borrowed an uninspected private sleeping space. Song Mei kept the eight printed sheets herself as the desk closed. Their departing potential buyers would not be quietly replaced by invented sales.

shoal_e05_oral_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_02.text: He Ming asked the listeners once more whether they wanted the short oral reprise. Both said yes. One chose the chair nearer the door because she planned to leave promptly afterward. The other asked to hear the coat song's opening again at its ordinary volume. Yue did not write a diagnosis explaining their preferences. They had offered listening needs, not private bodily histories for a public account. Song Mei could adapt the offered piece without demanding more.

shoal_e05_oral_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_03.text: The woman near the door had mended work gloves for years and knew the sound of a joke that would feel different when carried home. She wanted the rhythm as well as the words. Song Mei sang the opening, then let the woman tap the table softly to find the beat. Yue moved a cup away from the tapping hand. Her assistance was ordinary, and its smallness gave the listener room to do the thing she had actually come for.

shoal_e05_oral_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_04.text: The second listener asked whether a line could be repeated more slowly. Song Mei spoke it and then sang it once, preserving the difference between the page's meaning and the performance's movement. The listener laughed at the brother asking for his wedding sash back. Yue had laughed earlier at the impossible loan of a sleeve. A small room made those differing reactions audible without requiring either person to stand and explain herself to an entire harbor audience.

shoal_e05_oral_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_05.text: Halfway through, someone knocked and asked whether another ticket holder could join. The keeper's posted limit and the offered private listening arrangement did not permit an extra audience to drift in. Yue explained that a separately offered later event might be public, then kept this door clear. The newcomer went away disappointed. Serving two people properly had excluded another spontaneous opportunity. Privacy had a real boundary, not simply a warmer name for openness.

shoal_e05_oral_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_06.text: The woman near the door offered a story about her own brother's coat. Song Mei asked whether she wanted to tell it privately here or permit any later retelling. She chose private telling only. Yue put her notebook away before the story began. It was funny and a little cruel, with a missing button everyone understood differently. The value of hearing it did not depend on exporting it. The woman left its funniest sentence inside this room.

shoal_e05_oral_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_07.text: The other listener asked for the coat song's words to be read once without music. Song Mei obliged within the offered short repertoire. Yue watched the artist's voice change when the tune was absent. It became almost conversational, and one line sounded sad where the performance had made it comic. No printed sheet could guarantee the same effect. The listener listened with her hands still and said she would remember enough for her own ordinary household telling.

shoal_e05_oral_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_08.text: Song Mei explained which current text she permitted for such household reading and which private stories remained unoffered. The listeners accepted the distinction. They did not receive a commercial print license or rights to the leaving piece. The eight printed sheets stayed unsold with Song Mei because the desk had closed. Their words remained available to her future choices, but tonight's audience had scattered. An oral event could succeed without generating the revenue the unchosen desk might have brought.

shoal_e05_oral_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_09.text: Yue checked the time quietly so Song Mei did not have to turn a finishing line into a clock announcement. When the agreed end approached, the artist offered one final repeated refrain and stopped. The listeners stood at their own pace with the route clear. One thanked the artist; the other thanked Yue for the cup she had moved. Neither gratitude made them ongoing witnesses or promised attendance at another event. They had received the hour they accepted.

shoal_e05_oral_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_10.text: The keeper inspected the chairs and closed the side room under its current evening terms. No private listener notes remained on the table. Song Mei paid Yue the offered two copper after the actual assistant work ended. Eighteen ticket copper less the fixed venue fee, musician wages, and print expense had left the artist four; this completed task left her two. No sheet sale had occurred tonight. The eight texts remained her stock, available for a future offered sale without an invented buyer.

shoal_e05_oral_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_11.text: Yue asked whether Song Mei regretted not staffing the desk. The artist said she had offered both possibilities knowing their costs and preferred not to be asked to justify her own generosity as a failed business calculation. She still needed earnings. She had also wanted these two listeners to hear the piece. Yue understood the rebuke. A careful budget could explain a consequence without deciding which part of another person's work deserved to exist.

shoal_e05_oral_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_12.text: Outside, a former potential sheet buyer asked where he could get the printed words tonight. Song Mei said the desk was closed and gave the public request channel for a later offered sale. He would leave the port tomorrow and declined the channel. His missed purchase remained missed. Yue did not reopen the unstaffed table after its keeper's hour. The oral reprise had served its actual listeners while losing a finite departing market.

shoal_e05_oral_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_13.text: They walked together as far as the lane junction. Song Mei said the private coat story would stay private, even though it was good enough to tempt an artist. Yue said she had put away the notebook and had no written account to circulate. The performer looked relieved rather than impressed. Trust sometimes meant removing a useful tool from reach at the right moment, then accepting the unrecorded space where another person's words could simply have been heard.

shoal_e05_oral_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_oral_14.text: Song Mei declined company farther because she wanted the remaining walk alone. Yue accepted the end of their task and their shared road. Two retained copper was a narrow evening margin, and two listeners had received an experience they wanted. Eight unsold sheets and a missed departing buyer remained facts too. None required the performer to produce a moral verdict before bed. Her independent future would be hers, whether or not Yue liked its next destination.

shoal_e05_after_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_01.text: The lane outside had grown quiet enough to hear someone sweeping behind a closed shop. Yue returned to her own paid lodging without an artist's script in her bag. Her two-copper task wage belonged to the completed evening, separate from five restoration settlements and every older fund. Song Mei's offer had given her work with a finite end. She liked knowing that friendship could continue after such an end without either woman pretending the payment had meant something larger.

shoal_e05_after_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_02.text: On the morning of Day Two Hundred Sixty-Six, the performance notice was still on the board, now marked completed. A child read the fictional tide keeper's title aloud and asked when he would return. The keeper removed yesterday's ticket strip and said the performer had not promised another date. The child looked disappointed. Yue helped reach the lower notice peg at ordinary waist height. She could preserve a readable public board without manufacturing the event its youngest reader wanted.

shoal_e05_after_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_03.text: At the market, Song Mei stood beside a stall of pears and argued with its seller about ripeness. They greeted Yue after settling the ordinary price. The artist had already paid for her lodgings from her own settled earnings and road purse; last night's remainder did not represent her entire financial life. She would not ask Yue to underwrite a route merely because one evening's figures were small. The two women bought their breakfasts separately.

shoal_e05_after_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_04.text: A review of the performance had appeared as a scrap near the board. It called the leaving piece evasive and the coat song frivolous. Song Mei read it once and laughed too sharply. Yue began to say the writer had misunderstood her, then stopped because she did not know the writer's reasons. The artist said she might care about a criticism without obeying it. She took the public scrap down only when the keeper removed unauthorized notices under the board's ordinary rules.

shoal_e05_after_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_05.text: Song Mei wanted to walk before her next appointment. Yue went with her along the licensed quay edge, keeping outside active rigging lanes. A heron waited on a piling and missed two strikes at fish before catching a third. Neither woman turned the first failures into an omen. Song Mei said the bird had better timing than her second verse after the interruption. Yue laughed because the performer had chosen the comparison herself and could still be irritated about the verse.

shoal_e05_after_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_06.text: Near the public stair, a sailor tried to offer Song Mei an audience aboard his moored vessel. Its owner had not licensed a performance room, and the invitation's generous price did not solve the exit problem. She declined. He said artists were becoming too particular. She replied that he could be particular about his boat's repairs without performing gratitude for every offered patch. Yue watched the sailor accept that answer reluctantly, then change the subject to weather.

shoal_e05_after_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_07.text: They sat where the path widened. Song Mei said the harbor liked a story that proved its repairs deserved applause. Her work could depict repair without certifying the people paying for it. Yue admitted that the same wish followed a small technical success: someone wanted the marked object to validate the whole institution. The artist asked whether Yue ever wanted that too. She did. It was easier to bear a narrow result when imagining a broad vindication waiting behind it.

shoal_e05_after_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_08.text: A public messenger asked Song Mei to perform free at the clinic that evening. The request described a worthwhile audience and omitted setup, voice rest, and the staff time needed to host it. She declined that date and asked for a scoped later offer if the clinic wanted one. Yue did not volunteer the artist's services as repayment for ordinary care. The messenger left with an actual refusal, which remained kinder than accepting a promise Song Mei could not keep.

shoal_e05_after_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_09.text: When their walk reached the packing room, He Ming invited Song Mei to discuss a later worker reading under ordinary room terms. She accepted a conversation next week, not the event itself. Yue was not required as mediator and would not automatically attend. The invitation she had heard did not make the discussion part of her restoration job. Their paths could keep crossing without every meeting becoming a task assigned to the person whose certificate drew the most attention.

shoal_e05_after_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_10.text: Song Mei asked about Yue's next destination after the six-week term. Yue had not accepted one. She would finish the remaining five performed shifts and settle any carried property first. She might seek another bounded task or leave with her own pack. Song Mei said an unchosen future could be a real state rather than a temporary problem that friends must solve. Yue found the sentence both comforting and difficult. She had learned to confuse readiness with having already said yes.

shoal_e05_after_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_11.text: The artist stood when her own appointment approached. She would discuss a different room, its pay, and the stories she actually wanted to offer. Yue could wish it well without guaranteeing a better keeper. They parted without a promise to travel together. Song Mei's refusal to become the harbor's grateful chronicler had not made her cold; it had left enough room for the private irritation, pleasure, and practical ambition Yue had seen this morning.

shoal_e05_after_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e05_after_12.text: Yue returned toward the receiving cupboard and the carrier desk. Day Two Hundred Sixty-Six had a concrete deadline for any Lark equipment she actually held. The last port shifts followed on the scheduled days, with their own wages and owner returns. Behind her, the performance room resumed its other uses. An evening had ended. The words that survived it would move only through the paths their owner had permitted, and some experiences would remain with the people who heard them.
